## ⭐ Sharpened by PR #19405 — the in-code copy is FIXED, so the frozen registry text is now the ONLY stale one

When this card was filed, the two-filter enumeration existed in both the runtime source and the ADR-0087 registry. PR #19405 (ruling item 2 of #17667, landed `0862063ba7`) **corrected the in-code copy on its own initiative**, verified by this seat:

| | on the parent `6af29010b9` | on `main` `0862063ba7` |
|---|---|---|
| ``this door applies the `status` / `type` `` (two filters) | **present** | gone |
| ```status` / `type` / `enabled` filters`` (three) | absent | **present** |

⇒ ⭐ **this card's remaining subject is now exactly the frozen text and nothing else.** Measured on `origin/main`, `filters on \`status\` / \`type\`` still lives in:

- `packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts` (the source string)
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.api__ListInstalledPackagesRequest__limit.ts`
- `content/docs/references/api/package-api.mdx` (generated from the first)

⚠️ That makes the card **cleaner, ⛔ not more urgent**: the enumeration a reader hits while reading the *code* is now right, and what remains is a **retirement record** — which may legitimately be frozen as written. ⛔ The first act is still to decide whether a superseded passage inside a dated record is amended at all.
